newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks flirt with record.
newsitem.headline: French stocks flirt with record.

text.p: French shares finished slightly higher on Tuesday, settling just below Friday's record close, after a quiet session.
"It's summer. Volumes are slowing down. The market isn't likely either to boom or collapse between now and the autumn," a portfolio manager said.
The CAC-40 index closed up 1.43 points, or 0.05 percent, at 3,023.63, just below their closing record of 3,025.94 set last Friday.
The CAC-40 July futures edged up to 3,025 from 3,024 at Monday's close.
The broader SBF120 index rose 1.16 point to 2,059.98.
The bourse came off its session highs after U.S. data showing a slight acceleration in the employment cost index during the second quarter.
Wall Street's early losses also pressured the market, which traders say is in a consolidation phase. Brokers said the CAC could shed 50 to 100 points from current levels without setting off alarms.
Volume was a brisk 8.7 billion francs, inflated by a block trade in Generale des Eaux representing 0.84 percent of the utility's capital.
Sanofi shares jumped 5.54 percent to 610 francs on reports the pharmaceuticals company was selling its 49.9 percent stake in the Nina Ricci perfume house.
Sanofi said it would unload the stake if Nina Ricci's founders decided to sell.

"Sanofi's asset selling raises expectations that Elf is preparing to sell (its Sanofi stake)," a broker said. Elf Aquitaine is Sanofi's majority shareholder and has said it could cut its stake below 50 percent.
